subject: Urgent: eastus2 KV-cache saturation causing throughput collapse – exec bridge requested
messages:

Cc: Novus Health Infra <infra@novushealth.com>

Subject: Production throughput collapse in eastus2 (tokens blocked)

Evelyn — we're seeing a sharp throughput drop and 5xx spikes starting ~08:50 PDT for a subset of our traffic pinned to eastus2. Application-level retries are going up and response latency for chat endpoints is up ~5-8x.

We've attached a light log bundle (small anonymized traces) and a short video of the client timeline. Can you confirm if there's a known maintenance or capacity event? This is impacting our scheduled patient notifications window.

Immediate asks:
- Can Redwood confirm whether requests are being routed to a degraded AZ or being queued?
- Any ETA for mitigation or recommended temporary routing we should activate on our side?

Teresa
Head of Platform, Novus Health

Teresa — thanks for the heads-up and the logs. We're investigating now. No scheduled maintenance in eastus2 from our side. Initial telemetry shows a sudden increase in KV-cache eviction rates and an accompanying token-generation queue growth for instances serving Novus traffic.

We're spinning up an interim exec bridge and looping in our routing/infra on-call. I will update you with an initial mitigation plan within 20 minutes. For now, please do not change client-side routing — we want to avoid mid-request state divergence.

Quick note: if you can push any additional traces that show repeatable failing request IDs, that will speed correlation.

Evelyn
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: [EXEC BRIDGE] eastus2 KV-cache saturation / throughput collapse — immediate actions

Team — opening an exec bridge (PagerDuty PDT-8812). Summary:
- Symptom: spike in KV-cache evictions on eastus2 model fleet -> token-generation queue growth -> 5xx and high latency for a subset of customers (not global).
- Impact: Novus Health (high-tier customer) experiencing critical throughput loss during a time-window.

Immediate actions:
1) Traffic steering: Jordan, please prepare an emergency cross-region steer policy to move Novus traffic to westus2 with warm-up capacity. Aim for a gradual 30% shift in 10-minute increments to avoid downstream overload.
2) Runtime: Soojin, confirm whether unexpected background compaction / GC ran on eastus2 hosts and if we can temporarily increase KV cache capacity on the affected instance pool.
3) Telemetry & rollback: Marissa, run a token-level cost/latency breakdown and enable short-term tracing for Novus routes.
4) Exec comms: Evelyn, draft the customer update (clear ETA and workaround).

Attachments: redwood-routing-metric-snapshot-09-11.csv (metric sample).

I'll host the bridge and pull infra on-call. If steering to westus2 is approved, we'll need an authorization note to satisfy capacity billing for reserve pool use.

-Hannah
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: [EXEC BRIDGE] eastus2 KV-cache saturation / throughput collapse — immediate actions

All — we've validated that warm westus2 capacity is available. Proposed plan:
- Start a controlled steer: 25% -> 50% -> 100% in 12-minute windows, monitor 95th latency and 5xx.
- Apply a temporary model-variant fallback (quantized lower-memory variant) for Novus traffic where acceptable to reduce KV cache pressure.
- Increase KV-cache limit + disable low-priority background compaction on affected hosts (can be rolled back in 30m).

Soojin: infra traces show a GC/compaction job fired on 09:01 that coincides with eviction spike. If we pause compaction, eviction rate drops in sim. Ready to patch config.

Evelyn: recommend language for customer update below — short, actionable, ETA ~40-60 minutes for full recovery depending on warm-up. Need explicit sign-off to begin cross-region steer (we will charge reserve minutes if we use Dedicated burst).

--
Jordan Blake
Head of Infra Ops, Redwood Inference

Teresa — quick update from our exec bridge: we identified a KV-cache compaction job that coincided with an abnormal eviction spike in eastus2. Immediate mitigations implemented:
- Paused compaction on affected hosts; KV eviction rate dropped and 95th latency is falling.
- Initiated controlled cross-region steer of Novus traffic to westus2 (25% -> 50% now; we will hold at 50% for warming then evaluate moving to 100%).
- Applied temporary model-variant fallback for non-critical routes to reduce memory pressure.

ETA: We expect to see steady recovery within 40-60 minutes; keeping the steer active until we confirm stable 95th latency and error rate. No configuration changes required on Novus side for the steer; we'll coordinate a full revert once validated.

Billing note: cross-region burst to westus2 will incur reserve pool usage for the duration; I'll follow up with a short memo for approval.

Please reply if you'd like a live bridge (we can keep the bridge open for 90 minutes). Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as P1 for your account.

Evelyn
